projects.title: Identifying the barriers to and beliefs of strength training in young adult women and evaluating the effectiveness of interventions that have sought to overcome barriers
Effectiveness of aerobic exercise and strength training on reducing low-density lipoprotein levels in overweight or obese adults with hypercholesterolemia.
projects.description:
The obesity epidemic has not been improved in the past decade; in fact it has only gotten worse. With the consistency of obesity in the world, health conditions such as high cholesterol are more prevalent. There have been several studies that identified a positive association between obesity and high cholesterol. While previous studies show that aerobic exercise leads to weight loss and an enhancement of cholesterol levels, there has not been an adequate study done on strength training and its potential to enhance blood lipid profiles. We therefore propose a study to examine the effectiveness of strength training on enhancing blood lipid profile (triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein, and high-density lipoprotein levels) and body composition in overweight or obese, hypercholesterolemia patients. The study design will be a randomized controlled trial. For this study, blood lipid profile, body composition, and body weight tests will be performed before and after the 3-month intervention. A total of sixty male and female subjects aged between 35-55 were recruited from the greater Philadelphia area. We hypothesize that strength training will enhance blood lipid profile and body composition. The comparison data from this study will be analyzed by performing a parametric, one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) in order to compare the pre/post data of the experimental groups and the control group. In addition, a non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis ANOVA on Ranks (one-way) will be performed in order to express the ordinal data. Statistical significance will be accepted at P < 0.05. 

*Note: this is a just a study proposal for a class.
